title: AF-School-final(B261)
description: Airframe school final practice exam covering pressurization systems, sheet-metal and wood structure, fasteners, flight control rigging, hydraulics, fuel systems, and inspection/regulatory requirements.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a primary purpose of cabin pressurization at high altitude?
options: Maintaining a physiologically safe cabin altitude for occupants
Reducing the effects of hypoxia at cruise altitude
questions.explanation: Pressurization exists to keep cabin altitude low enough for occupant safety and comfort; noise insulation is a separate function (handled by soundproofing materials), not a purpose of the pressurization system itself.

questions.question: Which property of a material describes its ability to resist surface damage such as scratching, abrasion, or penetration?
questions.explanation: Hardness is the property that measures a material's resistance to localized surface damage like scratching, denting, or abrasion.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of the BITE (Built-In Test Equipment) function in a cabin pressure control system?
options: Detecting faults in the pressure controller and related sensors
Allowing maintenance personnel to verify system operation on the ground
questions.explanation: BITE is designed to self-test and detect faults within the pressurization control system; it is not intended to perform a general cabin temperature check at all altitudes, which is a function of the environmental control/temperature control system.

questions.question: The rate of change of cabin pressure (climb/descent) is indicated to the crew by the:
options: Cabin rate of change indicator (cabin vertical speed indicator)
questions.explanation: The cabin vertical speed indicator (cabin rate-of-climb/descent indicator) shows how quickly cabin pressure altitude is changing, similar to how an aircraft VSI shows altitude change rate.

questions.question: If a leak is found at a fuel system component joint, what is a correct corrective action?
options: Apply additional sealant over the leak without disturbing the joint
Torque the assembly bolts evenly to the specified value
Increase fuel system pressure to force the leak closed
questions.explanation: A leak at a joint is often due to uneven or insufficient bolt torque; evenly torquing the assembly bolts to the specified value is the correct corrective action rather than masking the leak with sealant.

questions.question: What is the best combination of reasons to defuel an aircraft?
options: Maintenance inspection, fuel contamination, and a change of flight plan
Only to reduce aircraft weight for towing
Only when the aircraft will be stored for more than a year
questions.explanation: Aircraft are commonly defueled for maintenance inspections requiring an empty tank, to remove contaminated fuel, or because a change in the flight plan means the loaded fuel is no longer appropriate.

questions.question: Which weather/cabin condition tends to cause a person's nasal cavity to become dry?
questions.explanation: Low humidity, common in pressurized cabin air at altitude, dries out the mucous membranes of the nasal cavity.

questions.question: On many pressurization systems, what is entered to allow the automatic system to schedule cabin pressure correctly for the trip?
options: The flight plan (cruise altitude/destination elevation) into the automatic pressurization controller
questions.explanation: The automatic cabin pressurization controller uses flight plan data, such as cruise altitude and destination field elevation, to schedule the cabin pressure profile for the flight automatically.

questions.question: The extension of the flat side of a formed part beyond the bend radius is called the:
questions.explanation: The mold line is the extension of the flat surfaces of a part beyond the radius, representing the theoretical sharp-cornered shape of the part before the bend radius was formed.

questions.question: Which of the following is a reusable temporary sheet metal fastener used to hold parts in alignment during assembly?
questions.explanation: A Cleco fastener is a reusable temporary spring-loaded fastener used to clamp sheet metal parts together through rivet holes during assembly, then removed and reused elsewhere.

questions.question: With a control cable system correctly rigged, the flight control surface should reach its mechanical stop:
options: Prior to the flight deck (cockpit) control reaching its stop
At the exact same instant as the flight deck control
Only after the flight deck control has reached its stop
questions.explanation: Correct rigging requires the control surface to contact its own stop slightly before the cockpit control reaches its stop, ensuring cable tension (not the cockpit control stop) limits surface travel.

questions.question: Airworthiness of an aircraft requires that the aircraft must conform to its:
options: Type certificate (and be in condition for safe operation)
questions.explanation: An aircraft is airworthy when it conforms to its type certificate (including applicable airworthiness directives and approved alterations) and is in a condition for safe operation.

questions.question: Which flight control tab assists the pilot only at high airspeeds?
questions.explanation: A spring tab is designed to assist control movement primarily at high airspeeds, where aerodynamic loads are high, by deflecting under a spring arrangement to reduce pilot effort.

questions.question: Aircraft that carry passengers along with crew must have seats that comply with which type of regulation?
questions.explanation: Passenger and crew seats must meet crashworthiness requirements, which address occupant protection and seat/restraint structural performance in the event of an accident.

questions.question: The overall purpose of aircraft inspection is to ensure that:
options: The paint and interior look new
The aircraft meets the owner's personal preferences
questions.explanation: Inspections exist to verify that the entire aircraft remains airworthy — safe and conforming to its approved design — not merely to check cosmetic condition.

questions.question: For wood classified as Class A (highest strength grade), what is the maximum allowable grain inclination?
questions.explanation: Class A wood (the highest quality grade) permits a grain slope no steeper than 1 in 15, reflecting its stricter strength requirements compared to lower grades.

questions.question: For wood classified as Class B, what is the maximum allowable grain inclination?
questions.explanation: Class B wood allows a slightly steeper maximum grain slope of 1 in 12, reflecting its somewhat lower strength grade compared to Class A.

questions.question: What is typically used to create a reinforced drain hole in sheet metal or fabric structure?
questions.explanation: Grommets are installed in drain holes to reinforce the edge of the hole and prevent chafing, cracking, or tearing of the surrounding material.

questions.question: On fixed-wing aircraft, nationality and registration marks are located:
options: On the vertical tail surfaces or the sides of the fuselage
On the top of the wing only
questions.explanation: Fixed-wing aircraft display their registration marks on the vertical tail surfaces (such as the rudder/fin) or on the sides of the fuselage, per standard marking location requirements.

questions.question: Who is responsible for updating the aircraft's weight and balance record after a major repair or alteration?
options: The repairman who performed the work
questions.explanation: The person (repairman/mechanic) who performs the major repair or alteration is responsible for updating the weight and balance record to reflect any resulting change in weight or CG.

questions.question: An uneven (unbalanced) quantity of fuel between wing tanks primarily affects which aspect of the aircraft's flight characteristics?
options: Directional (yaw) trim only, with no effect on roll
questions.explanation: Unequal fuel load between left and right tanks creates a lateral weight imbalance, which affects the aircraft's lateral (roll) stability and requires aileron/roll trim correction.

questions.question: What landing gear component is attached to the aircraft structure in such a way that the gear can pivot from the extended (vertical) position used for landing/taxi to the stowed position used in flight?
questions.explanation: The trunnion is the pivot mounting that attaches the landing gear leg to the aircraft structure, allowing it to rotate between the extended position and the retracted/stowed position.

questions.question: Which hydraulic valve directs pressurized fluid to one end of an actuating cylinder while simultaneously directing return fluid from the other end back to the reservoir?
questions.explanation: A selector valve directs pressurized fluid to one side of a double-acting actuator while simultaneously opening a return path from the opposite side back to the reservoir, allowing the actuator to move in the selected direction.

questions.question: Which component is used to prevent the extrusion of an O-ring seal under high hydraulic pressure?
questions.explanation: Backup rings are installed alongside an O-ring to fill the extrusion gap and prevent the O-ring material from being forced (extruded) into that gap under high pressure.

questions.question: What term describes the seals used in an assembly consisting of a cylinder with a moving piston inside it?
questions.explanation: Seals used between a moving piston and cylinder bore are generally referred to as packing, as distinguished from gaskets, which seal between two stationary mating surfaces.

questions.question: When removing and installing (torquing) a fitting on a flexible hydraulic hose, what should be done?
options: Use two wrenches/spanners to prevent the hose from twisting
Apply heat to loosen the fitting before removal
Always cut the hose rather than unscrewing the fitting
questions.explanation: Using two wrenches — one to hold the hose fitting and one to turn the connecting nut — prevents the flexible hose itself from twisting as the fitting is tightened or loosened.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a source of ignition?
options: Static discharge (via a properly installed static discharger/wick)
questions.explanation: Static dischargers (static wicks) are specifically designed to safely bleed off static electricity into the air, preventing the buildup that could otherwise create a spark — so a properly functioning static discharge is not itself a source of ignition.

questions.question: An aircraft owner may apply for authorization of a progressive inspection program to:
options: The concerned FAA Flight Standards District Office (FSDO)
questions.explanation: Authorization for a progressive inspection program is requested from and approved by the responsible FAA Flight Standards District Office (FSDO) with jurisdiction over the aircraft.

questions.question: What is required to legally fly an aircraft whose annual inspection has expired, to a location where the inspection can be performed?
options: A special flight permit (ferry permit) issued by the FAA
Verbal permission from any certificated mechanic
Nothing additional is required as long as the flight is short
questions.explanation: An aircraft with an expired annual inspection is not airworthy for normal flight, so a special flight (ferry) permit must be obtained from the FAA to legally fly it to a location where the inspection can be completed.

questions.question: Which nondestructive inspection method uses high-frequency sound waves to detect flaws within a material?
questions.explanation: Ultrasonic inspection uses high-frequency sound waves transmitted into the material; reflections from internal flaws or back surfaces are analyzed to detect subsurface defects.
